desk.headline: Headline EPS up to 155 US cents from 132c on higher gold price as output falls 9%; 2026 production guidance reaffirmed
results: Headline earnings per share rose to 155 US cents from 132c and profit attributable to shareholders to $787m from $669m; nine-month headline EPS was 606c (346c).
A received gold price of $4,239/oz (up from $3,490) offset a 9% fall in output to 696koz, driven by lower grades and problems at Sukari, Iduapriem and Obuasi.
All-in sustaining costs rose to $2,170/oz from $1,720/oz.
Free cash flow was $722m (from $920m) and net cash rose to $1.26bn from $231m a year earlier.
Interim dividend of 71 US cents ($361m) takes 2026 dividends declared to 259c; a buyback of up to $2.0bn has shareholder and Reserve Bank approval.

guidance.summary: AngloGold reaffirmed 2026 production of 2.80–3.17Moz and expects costs and capital spending to stay within the guided ranges, relying on a stronger fourth quarter.

points: CEO Alberto Calderon highlighted the group's quality and free cash flow generation.
Management expects a strong final quarter as Iduapriem dewatering reopens high-grade ore, Sukari stripping reaches better grades and Obuasi stopes ramp up again.
Obuasi is targeted at an annualised run rate of about 300koz in Q4.
The company put about 83% of the rise in AISC down to outside factors such as price-linked royalties and energy.
The board approved execution funding for North Bullfrog in Nevada on 3 Nov, subject to permits.
call.source: Q3 2026 earnings release (Form 6-K) commentary and Finviz, 5 Nov 2026 (no call transcript found)

watch: Whether Q4 output is strong enough to land inside the 2.80–3.17Moz range.
Recovery at Obuasi, Iduapriem and Sukari, and the trend in AISC.
Use of the $2.0bn buyback and Nevada project permits.
